title: Proactive and reactive engagement of artificial intelligence methods for education: a review
extended_summary:
This paper reviews how artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) have been used across the end-to-end education process, with a particular focus on distinguishing proactive uses from reactive uses. The authors ask how AI has been applied in education over the past two decades, how the COVID-19 pandemic affected the field, how datasets and algorithms have evolved, and whether AI has helped bridge or widen gaps in access to quality education.

The review is organized around a new categorization of AI engagement in education. Proactive engagement includes student admissions, curriculum and content design, timetabling, and content generation. Reactive engagement includes tutoring aids, performance assessment and monitoring, and outcome prediction. The paper synthesizes 195 original research articles published from 2003 to 2022, identified through a Google Scholar-based search and screened using explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria.

The review covers a broad educational context spanning classroom and online learning, administrative decision-making, tutoring systems, assessment tools, and content-generation systems. It discusses representative techniques such as logistic regression, decision trees, neural networks, reinforcement learning, NLP, and deep learning, and notes that modern AI has increasingly been used to automate and personalize educational processes. The main conclusion is that AI in education has expanded substantially and become more sophisticated over time, but there remain important infrastructural, fairness, transparency, privacy, and ethical challenges for widespread adoption.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: Intelligent Tutoring Systems are AI-driven educational systems that provide instruction, hints, feedback, personalization, and adaptive support during learning.
identified_tools.use_case: This systematic review synthesizes prior research on intelligent tutoring systems as one of the major reactive AI approaches in education, including interactive, personalized, affect-aware, and learning-style-aware tutoring aids.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems create educational content such as questions, problems, answers, and other instructional materials from prompts or source material.
identified_tools.use_case: The review mentions generative AI only as an emerging context in the background and contrasts it with earlier non-generative AI approaches; it does not empirically evaluate a specific generative tool.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review, but it does not evaluate a single AI tool with empirical outcomes in the paper excerpt provided. The paper synthesizes heterogeneous prior studies across categories rather than reporting a direct intervention study of one system.
impact_tier_rationale: The review indicates broad and important relevance for lesson planning and instructional decisions, especially in proactive design and reactive tutoring applications. However, no single effect size or outcome magnitude is reported in this paper excerpt, so impact remains indirect and difficult to quantify.
